headline: Harmonic Security, a start-up that polices how employees use AI tools at work, has raised $50 million in new funding.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 7: fresh announcement, confirmed by the company; funding for AI-use security is a clear trend.
importance_line: Companies worried about staff pasting sensitive data into AI tools get another dedicated product, though the article gives no independent test of how well it works.
summary: SecurityWeek reports that Harmonic Security, a US start-up whose software watches and controls how employees use AI tools, announced a $50 million Series B round led by Crosspoint Capital Partners, taking its total funding to $76 million. The money will be used to hire engineers and sales staff in the US and UK, and the product covers browser-based AI, desktop AI tools and AI agents, using small language models to read each AI interaction in context.
notes: Company announcement; effectiveness claims are Harmonic's own.
